# About this release

This release builds on version 2.4.0.1 with a large number of bug fixes, and adds three new features: incremental (delta) backups of Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, and restore tests that can run after backups and be switched on remotely from the console.

The local database format is updated by this release. See "Downgrading" below before going back to an earlier version.

## Delta walk for Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace

Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace backups no longer need to list every item on every run. The providers now store a delta token with each backup and use the Microsoft Graph and Google change APIs, so later backups list only what was created, changed, moved or removed since the previous backup and carry the rest forward from it.

For Microsoft 365 this covers mail folders, SharePoint and group document libraries. For Google Workspace it covers Gmail, Drive, Calendar and Contacts. Delta tracking is enabled by default. The first backup, the first backup after the local database is recreated, and the backup after one that was stopped still list everything in full.

Delta tracking can be turned off per service with `--office365-disable-mail-delta`, `--office365-disable-drive-delta`, `--google-disable-gmail-delta`, `--google-disable-drive-delta`, `--google-disable-calendar-delta` and `--google-disable-contacts-delta`. If a document library reports more changes than `--office365-drive-delta-max-items` or `--google-drive-delta-max-items`, the library is listed in full instead.

A backup that combines a Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace source with the USN change journal or `--changed-files` is now refused with an error, as the two mechanisms cannot be combined.

## Restore tests

A new restore test operation restores a sample of a backup from the remote destination into a temporary folder and verifies it, so the backup is regularly proven to be restorable. It is available as the `restore-test` command in the command line and in ServerUtil, and through the server API.

The sample is chosen with `--restore-test-mode`: a number of random files, a percentage of the backup size, every file, or a rolling mode that prefers files that have not been verified recently. The test can be limited with `--restore-test-max-download-size` and `--restore-test-max-runtime`, can rebuild a temporary database from the destination with `--restore-test-recreate-database`, and can compare the restored files with the source files with `--restore-test-compare-source`.

Set `--perform-restore-test-after` to run a restore test as the last step of a backup whenever the previous test is older than the given interval. When the machine is connected to the Duplicati console, the console can set this interval for its backups, so restore tests can be switched on remotely. A restore test after a backup does not change the result of the backup, but a failed test is reported with its own notification.

## Improved support for Sync jobs

With this version, Sync jobs now store their logs so the logs can be viewed after the job has completed. Several places where the Sync job was showing options that were only relevant to restores are now updated.

## Other new features

- Backup versions can be given a label with the `set-version-label` command. The labels are also stored on the destination, so a database recreate keeps them.
- Point-in-time access to a destination: with `--remote-point-in-time`, the S3 and Duplicati Storage destinations read the destination as it was at the given time, using bucket versioning. The destination is read-only in this mode.
- Report modules can send reports for other operations than backups, chosen with `--send-http-operations`, `--send-mail-operations`, `--send-xmpp-operations` and `--send-telegram-operations`. Backup reports remain the default.
- A restore on an existing backup can now carry additional advanced options.
- The new `--disable-secret-provider` option disables the default secret provider, the configured secret provider, or both. `--disable-default-secret-provider` still works but is deprecated. The server now also reports which secret provider is active.
- Duplicati Storage can be used as a secondary target, and supports object locking.
- Uploads to Google Cloud Storage now carry a CRC32 checksum.
- SMB servers that require SMB 3.1.1 can be used with `--enable-smb311`.
- Neon Object Storage has been added to the list of S3 providers.

## Changed behavior

- A backup that asks for object locks on a bucket or container that does not have locking enabled now completes with a warning that no locks were applied, instead of failing. This applies to S3, B2, Azure, Google Cloud Storage and Duplicati Storage.
- Options in source and destination urls are now validated, so an option that no module supports is reported with a warning.
- The Microsoft 365 site classifications "Classic" and "Communication" have been removed, as they never matched any site.
- When a restore does not specify overwrite, restore permissions or skip metadata, the settings of the backup and the server defaults now apply instead of turning them off.

## Downgrading

This release updates the local database from version 19 to version 22 and the sync database to version 1. Version 2.4.0.1 cannot open the newer databases. To go back to 2.4.0.1, downgrade the databases with the DatabaseTool `downgrade` command first. Its default target versions now match 2.4.0.1, so no version options are needed.

## Fixes

Aborting a backup no longer waits for a stuck source listing, file open, size or metadata read, and a stop or abort that arrives before the operation is ready is kept.

Restores keep an appended file when restoring without `--overwrite`, do not read through a link when restoring a symbolic link to a file, keep the drive letter folder when restoring Windows paths in place, and stop when `--restore-path` has no value. A partial restore no longer warns about the folders it has to create. Repair keeps the time and order of the versions when it replaces missing dlist files, and a later database recreate keeps them too.

On Windows, a local folder destination whose url contains `@` or carries options in its query string is now read correctly, and symbolic links created by WSL are backed up as links. Backups leave the write-ahead log files of their own database out.

The server and tray icon have fixes to notifications, task state, pause and resume events, preload settings, update checks, the login token cookie behind a reverse proxy, and the Agent. Control file restores are protected against path traversal, and the recovery tool and the Agent pre-shared key have been hardened.

Backend fixes include Jottacloud timeouts and parallel downloads, Storj uploads, WebDAV listings on Windows and Linux, the S3 list API version option, HashiCorp Vault JSON secrets, GnuPG on slow systems, and the User-Agent header sent by WebDAV, pCloud and the updater.

SQLite has been updated to 3.54.0, built for older Linux distributions, and StreamJsonRpc and MimeKit have been updated for security advisories.
